introduction: This spec defines the `GitLabPlatform` concrete implementation of `PlatformProtocol` in the `afissues` package, along with shared SSRF/HTTP utilities and platform factory updates, enabling agent-fox to manage GitLab issues, labels, and merge requests with the same interface used for GitHub. Note: requirements referencing `afissues.protocol`, `afissues.errors`, and `GitHubPlatform` APIs are based on PRD descriptions of spec 03 (`03_extract_platform_afissues`) and should be cross-checked against the installed package before implementation.

glossary.ConfigError: Exception class in `afissues.errors` raised when the platform is misconfigured (e.g., invalid URL, missing token, SSRF violation).
glossary.GITEA_TOKEN: Environment variable holding the Gitea personal access token used by the platform factory.
glossary.GITHUB_TOKEN: Environment variable holding the GitHub personal or installation access token used by the platform factory.
glossary.GITLAB_TOKEN: Environment variable holding the GitLab personal or project access token used by the platform factory.
glossary.GitHubPlatform: Existing concrete implementation of `PlatformProtocol` in `afissues/github.py`, targeting the GitHub REST API.
glossary.GitLabPlatform: New concrete implementation of `PlatformProtocol` in `afissues/gitlab.py`, targeting the GitLab REST API v4.
glossary.GiteaPlatform: Future concrete implementation of `PlatformProtocol` for Gitea, introduced by the `gitea_platform` spec; only a lazy-import stub exists in the factory after this spec.
glossary.IntegrationError: Exception class in `afissues.errors` raised when an external API call returns an unexpected HTTP status or connectivity error.
glossary.IssueComment: Dataclass defined in `afissues.protocol` representing a platform-agnostic issue comment, with fields: `id`, `body`, `user`, `created_at`.
glossary.IssueResult: Dataclass defined in `afissues.protocol` representing a platform-agnostic issue, with fields: `number`, `title`, `html_url`, `body`, `labels`.
glossary.PRIVATE-TOKEN: GitLab HTTP request header used for authentication, carrying a personal access token or project access token.
glossary.PlatformProtocol: Abstract base class/protocol defined in `afissues.protocol` that declares the 12 standard methods all platform implementations must fulfil.
glossary.SSRFGuardTransport: Custom `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport` subclass in `afissues/_ssrf.py` that rejects requests targeting private/loopback/link-local IP addresses.
glossary._SUPPORTED_PLATFORMS: Module-level constant in `platform_factory.py` listing the valid platform type strings.
glossary._check_address: Function in `afissues/_ssrf.py` that raises `ConfigError` when an address violates SSRF constraints.
glossary._http.py: Shared internal module `afissues/_http.py` containing the `request_with_retry` async function extracted from `GitHubPlatform._request`.
glossary._ssrf.py: Shared internal module `afissues/_ssrf.py` containing SSRF guard utilities extracted from `afissues/github.py`.
glossary._validate_transport_address: Function in `afissues/_ssrf.py` that validates a resolved host address for SSRF safety.
glossary._validate_url: Function in `afissues/_ssrf.py` that validates a URL string for SSRF safety.
glossary.add_labels: GitLab issue update API field accepting a comma-separated string of label names to add to an issue.
glossary.afissues: Python package housing the platform abstraction layer, protocol definitions, error types, and platform implementations.
glossary.api: GitLab personal access token scope granting full read/write REST API access; the minimum required scope for `GitLabPlatform`.
glossary.backoff_base: Parameter to `request_with_retry` specifying the base delay in seconds for exponential backoff between retry attempts.
glossary.create_platform: Factory function in `platform_factory.py` that constructs and returns a `PlatformProtocol` instance.
glossary.create_platform_safe: Factory function in `platform_factory.py` that constructs a `PlatformProtocol` instance, suppressing or wrapping errors for safe callers.

user_story.goal: instantiate GitLabPlatform with a project path, token, and optional host URL
user_story.benefit: so that the platform connects to the correct GitLab project with authenticated requests and SSRF protection

acceptance_criteria.action: exposes class attribute `forge_type` equal to `"gitlab"`, accepts constructor arguments `project_id: str`, `token: str`, and `url: str = "gitlab.com"`, URL-encodes `project_id` internally (e.g. `"group/subgroup/project"` becomes `"group%2Fsubgroup%2Fproject"`), sets API base URL to `https://{url}/api/v4`, and stores auth headers as `{"PRIVATE-TOKEN": token}`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Instance is created successfully with all attributes set; no exception raised for valid inputs

acceptance_criteria.action: calls `_validate_url` from `_ssrf.py` and raises `ConfigError` before any HTTP client is created
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `ConfigError` is raised with a message indicating the SSRF violation
acceptance_criteria.trigger: receives a `url` value that resolves to a private, loopback, or link-local IP address

acceptance_criteria.action: uses `httpx.AsyncClient` with `SSRFGuardTransport` and the timeout configuration from `request_with_retry`; each request creates a new client via `async with httpx.AsyncClient(...)` inside `request_with_retry` rather than holding a persistent client
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: No persistent client state is held between method calls

acceptance_criteria.action: includes a module docstring that documents the minimum required GitLab token scope as `api`, and explains that tokens with only `read_api` scope will receive 403 errors on write operations
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Docstring is present and references the `api` scope requirement

acceptance_criteria.action: is re-exported from `afissues/__init__.py` alongside `GitHubPlatform`, making it importable as `from afissues import GitLabPlatform`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Import succeeds without error

edge_cases.action: raises `ConfigError` immediately without constructing the HTTP client; does not raise `IntegrationError`
edge_cases.error_condition: `url` is a string that URL-parses to a private RFC-1918 address (e.g. `"192.168.1.1"`)

edge_cases.action: URL-encodes the path internally using standard percent-encoding; callers pass the raw path unchanged
edge_cases.return_contract: API URLs are correctly formed with encoded path segments
edge_cases.error_condition: `project_id` contains characters that require URL percent-encoding (e.g. slashes, spaces)

user_story.goal: create a new issue on a GitLab project
user_story.benefit: so that the fix-pipeline can open tracked work items on GitLab the same way it does on GitHub

acceptance_criteria.action: sends `POST /api/v4/projects/{project_id}/issues` with JSON body `{"title": title, "description": body, "labels": ",".join(labels)}` and auth header `PRIVATE-TOKEN`; on HTTP 201 maps response fields `iid` → `number`, `web_url` → `html_url`, `description` (defaulting to `""` if null) → `body`, `labels` array → `labels` tuple, `title` → `title`, and returns an `IssueResult`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `IssueResult` with all five fields populated; raises `IntegrationError` on non-201 response

edge_cases.action: raises `IntegrationError` with response text truncated to 500 characters
edge_cases.error_condition: GitLab API returns a non-201 HTTP status (e.g. 422 validation error, 403 forbidden)

edge_cases.action: defaults `body` field of the returned `IssueResult` to `""`
edge_cases.error_condition: GitLab API response includes `description: null`

user_story.goal: retrieve issues filtered by label, state, and sort order from a GitLab project
user_story.benefit: so that the pipeline can query its tracked issues the same way it does on GitHub

acceptance_criteria.action: sends `GET /api/v4/projects/{project_id}/issues` with query params: `labels=label`, `state` mapped (`"open"` → `"opened"`, `"closed"` and `"all"` passed through), `order_by` mapped from `sort` (`"created"` → `"created_at"`, `"updated"` → `"updated_at"`), `sort` set to `direction` value (`"asc"` or `"desc"` passed through), and `per_page=100`; maps each response element to `IssueResult` using the standard field mapping
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: List of `IssueResult` objects on HTTP 200; raises `IntegrationError` on non-200

acceptance_criteria.action: maps protocol `state` value `"open"` to GitLab API value `"opened"`; passes `"closed"` and `"all"` through to GitLab unchanged
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Correct `state` query parameter sent to GitLab API

acceptance_criteria.action: maps protocol `sort` value `"created"` to GitLab `order_by` value `"created_at"` and `"updated"` to `"updated_at"`; maps `direction` values `"asc"` and `"desc"` directly to GitLab's `sort` parameter unchanged
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Correct `order_by` and `sort` query parameters sent to GitLab API

edge_cases.action: raises `IntegrationError` with response text truncated to 500 characters

correctness_properties.title: Field mapping completeness: IssueResult fields sourced only from documented GitLab API fields
correctness_properties.invariant: Fields are populated exclusively from `iid` → `number`, `title` → `title`, `web_url` → `html_url`, `description` → `body` (defaulting to `""`), and `labels` array → `labels` tuple; no extra GitLab-specific fields appear in the `IssueResult`

correctness_properties.title: Field mapping completeness: IssueComment fields sourced only from documented GitLab API fields
correctness_properties.invariant: Fields are populated exclusively from `id` → `id`, `body` → `body`, `author.username` → `user`, `created_at` → `created_at`; no extra GitLab-specific fields appear in the `IssueComment`

correctness_properties.title: SSRF safety: no requests to private/loopback addresses
correctness_properties.invariant: Every HTTP request passes through `SSRFGuardTransport`; no request is ever sent to a private RFC-1918, loopback, or link-local IP address; SSRF violations raise `ConfigError` at construction time

correctness_properties.title: Retry boundedness: request_with_retry never exceeds max_retries attempts
correctness_properties.invariant: The total number of HTTP attempts never exceeds `max_retries` (default 3) regardless of how many consecutive transient errors occur; after the last attempt the exception is re-raised

correctness_properties.title: Idempotency: create_label always returns None including on 409
correctness_properties.invariant: `create_label` returns `None` and raises no exception whether the label is newly created (201) or already exists (409); any other non-2xx status raises `IntegrationError`

correctness_properties.title: System notes excluded: list_issue_comments never returns system-generated notes
correctness_properties.invariant: Every `IssueComment` in the returned list corresponds to a GitLab note where `system == false`; no system-generated activity notes appear in the output regardless of API response content

correctness_properties.title: parse_remote never raises exceptions for any input
correctness_properties.invariant: `parse_remote` either returns a `tuple[str, str]` or `None`; it never raises any exception regardless of the input value

correctness_properties.title: No persistent HTTP client state between GitLabPlatform method calls
correctness_properties.invariant: No `httpx.AsyncClient` instance is retained as instance state after any method call completes; every `request_with_retry` invocation creates and closes its own client via `async with httpx.AsyncClient(...)`

correctness_properties.title: Factory module loads without error regardless of afissues.gitea availability
correctness_properties.invariant: The factory module always imports successfully even when `afissues/gitea.py` does not exist; `ImportError` for Gitea is only raised at runtime when a Gitea platform is actually requested

execution_paths.title: End-to-end: agent-fox nightshift creates and labels a GitLab issue

steps.action: reads platform config with `platform.type = "gitlab"`, calls `create_platform()` in `platform_factory.py`
reads `GITLAB_TOKEN` from environment, calls `afissues.gitlab.parse_remote` on the git remote URL to resolve `project_id`, constructs `GitLabPlatform(project_id, token, url)`
calls `_validate_url` from `_ssrf.py` to check for SSRF violations, URL-encodes `project_id`, stores auth headers as `{"PRIVATE-TOKEN": token}`
calls `platform.create_issue(title, body, labels)` on the returned `GitLabPlatform` instance

calls `request_with_retry` from `_http.py` to send `POST /api/v4/projects/{project_id}/issues` with `description`, `title`, and comma-joined `labels`; retries on transient network errors up to 3 times with exponential backoff
creates `httpx.AsyncClient` with `SSRFGuardTransport` from `_ssrf.py`, sends the POST request, returns `httpx.Response`
maps GitLab response fields (`iid` → `number`, `web_url` → `html_url`, `description` → `body`, `labels` array → tuple) and returns `IssueResult`
calls `platform.assign_label(issue_number, label)` to add a workflow label to the created issue
calls `request_with_retry` to send `PUT /api/v4/projects/{project_id}/issues/{iid}` with `{"add_labels": label}`; returns normally on HTTP 200
observes `IssueResult` with the new issue URL and confirms the workflow label is applied

execution_paths.title: End-to-end: agent-fox nightshift opens a merge request on GitLab with duplicate handling

steps.action: calls `platform.create_pr(title, body, head_branch, base_branch)` on an existing `GitLabPlatform` instance
calls `request_with_retry` to send `POST /api/v4/projects/{project_id}/merge_requests` with `source_branch`, `target_branch`, `title`, `description`
returns HTTP 409 Conflict because a merge request already exists for the same `source_branch` and `target_branch`
calls `request_with_retry` to send `GET /api/v4/projects/{project_id}/merge_requests?source_branch={head}&target_branch={base}&state=opened`
returns HTTP 200 with a list containing the existing open merge request
extracts `web_url` from the first result and returns it to the caller
receives the merge request URL and records it in the issue as a comment via `platform.add_issue_comment`

execution_paths.title: End-to-end: agent-fox nightshift closes a GitLab issue with a comment

steps.action: calls `platform.close_issue(issue_number, comment_text)` on an existing `GitLabPlatform` instance
detects non-empty `comment_text` and calls `add_issue_comment(issue_number, comment_text)` first
calls `request_with_retry` to send `POST /api/v4/projects/{project_id}/issues/{iid}/notes` with `{"body": comment_text}`; returns normally on HTTP 201
calls `request_with_retry` to send `PUT /api/v4/projects/{project_id}/issues/{iid}` with `{"state_event": "close"}`
returns HTTP 200; issue is now in `closed` state
observes successful return from `close_issue`; workflow completes

execution_paths.title: SSRF violation blocked at platform construction time

steps.action: calls `create_platform()` with `platform.type = "gitlab"` and `platform.url = "192.168.1.100"`
constructs `GitLabPlatform(project_id, token, url="192.168.1.100")`
calls `_validate_url("192.168.1.100")` from `_ssrf.py`; `_check_address` detects private IP and raises `ConfigError`
propagates `ConfigError` to the caller; no HTTP client is created; no network activity occurs
receives `ConfigError` and surfaces it as a configuration error to the operator

receives `ConfigError` and surfaces it as a configuration error
